title: Together in practice
hook: an old couple asks the Buddha to meet again in the next life; his answer, and a week of family looked back on
tomorrow: and when love ends in a goodbye, what does kindness look like?

segments.voice: Yesterday, not owning: metta wishes someone happy without claiming them. Today, two people who loved that way for a lifetime, and asked for one more.

Can an old couple meet again in the next life? Two of the Buddha's lay followers asked him exactly that. They're known by their son's name: Nakula's father and Nakula's mother. He speaks first. She was brought to my home when we were both young, and in all the years since, I don't recall wronging her, not even in thought. We want to see each other in this life, and in the next. Then she says the same, almost word for word.
screen: `MEET AGAIN NEXT LIFE?` → `NAKULA'S FATHER AND MOTHER.` → `NOT EVEN IN THOUGHT.`

segments.voice: The Buddha's answer is simple. If two people want to meet in this life and the next, let them be matched: the same faith, saddha, the same virtue, the same generosity, the same wisdom. Then they will. Notice what he doesn't say: be the same personality, want the same things, never disagree. He names four qualities to grow side by side. And he doesn't scold them for wanting more time, or call their wish clinging. He takes an old couple's love seriously, and tells them what feeds it. Faith keeps them facing the same way. Virtue keeps them trustworthy to each other. Generosity keeps their hands open. Wisdom keeps them seeing clearly, even as they change. This couple shared one path. Some readers in families of two traditions hear the sutta as asking for that match in trust, goodness, giving and wisdom, practiced together. And that's where the week ends up. Repair quickly: see the fault, make amends, hold back after. East: parents, with duties running both ways. Hard to repay: goodness shared is the coin that counts. Kind and clear: a warm hand and steady feet. West: partners guarding one house from both sides. Not owning: metta, an open hand. Together is where all six lead: two people growing the same good things, side by side, for as long as they get.
screen: `MATCHED IN FOUR THINGS.` · `FAITH, VIRTUE, GIVING, WISDOM.` · `NOT THE SAME PERSONALITY.` · `A WEEK OF FAMILY.` · then, large: `TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: If someone you share a life with is nearby, sit these two minutes side by side, no talking, just breathing in the same room. If you're alone, bring one person to mind and sit as though they were beside you. Let your breathing settle next to theirs. Nothing to fix, nothing to say; just two lives in one room for a little while.
Together in practice: two people matched in faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom, the Buddha's answer to Nakula's parents, who wanted one more life side by side.
Keep this one: together, growing the same good things side by side. Six of eleven, and the week is closed.

screen: `DAY 1596 COUNTS.` → `FAMILY · 6 OF 11.` → `TOMORROW: WHEN LOVE ENDS IN A GOODBYE?`

what a scholar hears: AN 4.55 (Samajivi Sutta) gives the couple's mutual declaration and the fourfold matching; Nakula's parents appear elsewhere in the canon as model lay followers.

chat.says: ava's grandparents danced at the wedding like teenagers. her grandma says they pray together every night. is that the secret?
options: Maybe part of it. The Buddha told an old couple: grow faith, virtue, giving and wisdom together.
No secret. Staying together is luck; what a couple practices has nothing to do with it.
It's the words. Say the same prayer every night and forever is guaranteed.
chat.meaning: The Buddha told Nakula's parents that a couple matched in faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom will meet again. Practicing together grows the match.

tie.story: The Buddha told Nakula's parents that a couple matched in faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom stays together.

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 4.55 (Samajivi Sutta: Nakula's father and Nakula's mother each say they have not transgressed against the other even in thought since she was brought to his home when both were young, and wish to see each other in this life and the next; the Buddha: if both have the same faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom, they will)
